title: A shadow elevation scale
summary: Three box-shadows, from resting to floating, each layered from a tight and a soft shadow.
explanation: Shadows suggest how far an element floats above the page. A small, sharp shadow sits close; a large, blurred, offset one floats high. Reuse a few levels instead of inventing a new shadow each time.
Each level here is two shadows, comma-separated: a tight one that anchors the card and a soft one for depth. Real shadows look like that, so the result feels more natural than one big blur.
Low-alpha black (rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1)) keeps the shadows soft; pure black looks like a smudge.
tryThis: Change the colour in .high's second shadow to rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6): harsh.
Remove the first (tight) shadow from .mid: it looks blurrier and less grounded.
Add a spread: change .low to 0 0 0 4px #fed7aa. Zero blur and a spread make a ring.
